text:
maria: heads-up — starting preflight observability sweep for embed-service rollout in the 10:30 change window. can people run quick checks?
ashwin: on it, running dashboards now. will check p95, errors, and kv-cache hit rate.
olivia: I'll watch the canary traces and span error % on jaeger.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: embed-service v2.4.0 -> canary (10% traffic). window: 10:30-11:30. CI: green.
ashwin: p95 baseline: 120ms. current canary p95: 190ms, +58%. not great.
olivia: seeing increased 5xxs from embeddings worker: rate at 0.7% (baseline 0.08%). stacktrace sample: `rpc: context deadline exceeded` repeated.
maria: ok that's above our canary guardrails. our rollback criteria were: p95 > 1.5x baseline for 3 consecutive minutes OR 5xx > 0.5% sustained for 2m.
jordan: can we narrow to a specific region? this only looks like us-east-1. routing shows fallback to cpu-hosts in eu is stable.
ashwin: confirmed region-scoped spike. KV-cache hit rate dropped from 85% -> 22% on canary nodes. that would explain token generation latency.
olivia: adding an alert: `canary.kv_hit_rate < 50% for 3m` and `canary.p95 > 1.5x baseline for 2m`.
monitoring-bot: Alert created: canary.p95_spike (threshold 1.5x) — firing in us-east-1. Link: https://console.redwood/s/alerts/AC-9832
maria: decision call: since both p95 and kv-hit dropped, we should rollback the canary to v2.3.8 and pin until we debug. any objections?
jordan: agree, don't want customer-facing impact. I'll run the rollback.
ashwin: before rollback — we can try draining canary nodes to warm caches? `kubectl rollout pause` and `kubectl scale deployment embed-service-canary --replicas=0` would spin down, but that still keeps traffic diverted.
maria: follow the standard rollback runbook: 1) abort canary rollout, 2) pin traffic to v2.3.8, 3) open a postmortem channel.
deploy-bot: Rollout aborted by jordan. Command: `redwoodctl rollout abort --service embed-service --env prod --reason "canary p95/kvcache regression"`
jordan: pinning to v2.3.8 now: `redwoodctl traffic set --service embed-service --version v2.3.8 --percent 100`
monitoring-bot: Traffic shift completed. Canary nodes drained. Firing alerts resolved: canary.p95_spike -> OK, canary.kv_hit_rate -> OK.
maria: thanks team. opening a 1-hour follow-up to investigate kv-cache change in v2.4.0 — suspect a serialized cache key change. olivia can you take the lead on traces?
olivia: on it. will collect traces and diff the cache key code path, and schedule a quick rollback postmortem in #postmortems.
maria: documented decisions and next steps in the release notes: noting rollback criteria hit, action taken, and contact points. :white_check_mark:
jordan: also adding an emergency tag to the v2.4.0 PR so it doesn't get re-promoted accidentally.
nashwin: for the immediate runbook improvement — propose we add a canary kv_hit_rate synthetic check to preflight scripts and failing fast before traffic split.
maria: agreed. create a follow-up ticket and add a preflight check in the pipeline.
olivia: copying logs and sample spans to the ticket. will post updates there.
monitoring-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0412-01 (canary kv-cache regression) assigned to olivia, priority P2.
maria: good catch everyone. closing this thread once the postmortem ticket is live.
